q-12786.name: Question 1
q-12786.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $p$ is $4{p}^{2}=25.$
q-12786.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and collect the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2} & =25 \\ 4{p}^{2}-25 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2}-25 & =0 \\ (2p)^{2}-{5}^{2} & =0 \\ (2p-5)(2p+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
2p-5=0\,\text{or}\,2p+5=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2p-5 & =0 & \, & \, & 2p+5 & =0 \\ 2p & =5 & \, & \, & 2p & =-5 \\ p & =\frac{5}{2} & \, & \, & p & =-\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $p=-\frac{5}{2},\frac{5}{2}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $p=\pm \frac{5}{2}.$

Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation p is 4p2=25.

a
p=0,52

p=2,5

p=−52
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and collect the like terms: 4p2=254p2−25=0

Now, using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation: 4p2−25=0(2p)2−52=0(2p−5)(2p+5)=0

Applying the zero product rule, we have 2p−5=0or2p+5=0.

Then, we solve each equation separately:

2p−5=02p+5=02p=52p=−5p=52p=−52

Therefore, the solutions are p=−52,52. We can write this even more concisely as p=±52.

q-44216.name: Question 2
q-44216.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $100{x}^{2}=7.$
q-44216.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and collect the like terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}100{x}^{2} & =7 \\ 100{x}^{2}-7 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}100{x}^{2}-7 & =0 \\ (10x)^{2}-{(\sqrt{7})}^{2} & =0 \\ (10x-\sqrt{7})(10x+\sqrt{7}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
10x-\sqrt{7}=0\,\text{or}\,10x+\sqrt{7}=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}10x-\sqrt{7} & =0 & \, & \, & 10x+\sqrt{7} & =0 \\ 10x & =\sqrt{7} & \, & \, & 10x & =-\sqrt{7} \\ x & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10} & \, & \, & x & =-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10},\frac{\sqrt{7}}{10}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $x=\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{10}.$

q-111997.name: Question 3
q-111997.problem: Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation $16{y}^{2}-81=0.$
q-111997.worked_solution:
Using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{y}^{2}-81 & =0 \\ (4y)^{2}-(9)^{2} & =0 \\ (4y-9)(4y+9) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the zero product rule, we have

$$
4y-9=0\,\text{or}\,4y+9=0.
$$

Then, we solve each equation separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y-9 & =0 & \, & \, & 4y+9 & =0 \\ 4y & =9 & \, & \, & 4y & =-9 \\ y & =\frac{9}{4} & \, & \, & y & =-\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=-\frac{9}{4},\frac{9}{4}.$ We can write this even more concisely as $y=\pm \frac{9}{4}.$

Question 3
?

Use the difference of squares method to solve the equation 16y2−81=0.

a
y=8116
b
y=29
c
y=±94
d
y=±92
e
y=±8116
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the difference of squares formula, we factor the left-hand side of our quadratic equation: 16y2−81=0(4y)2−(9)2=0(4y−9)(4y+9)=0

Applying the zero product rule, we have 4y−9=0or4y+9=0.

Then, we solve each equation separately: 4y−9=04y+9=04y=94y=−9y=94y=−94

Therefore, the solutions are y=−94,94. We can write this even more concisely as y=±94.
